sourceCopy.name: Hiking Time Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Hiking Time Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Estimate hiking hours from total route distance, uphill gain, a Naismith baseline or your own pace, and planned breaks.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter the total route distance and cumulative uphill gain. Compare a simple Naismith-style baseline with a pace you choose, then add planned rest breaks.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How does this hiking time estimate work?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Moving time is total distance divided by your chosen pace. The Naismith-style baseline uses 5 km/h plus 10 minutes per 100 m of cumulative ascent. Custom mode uses your entered pace and climb allowance. Planned breaks are added separately.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Is my route uploaded or saved?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The estimate runs in this browser and your route inputs are not uploaded or saved.

fields.climbRate: Added minutes per 100 m of ascent
fields.breakRate: Planned break minutes per hiking hour
fields.breakHint: Breaks are estimated from moving time and shown separately; add only the rest you plan to take.
fields.accuracyNote: A planning estimate, not a route-specific prediction. It does not model descent, terrain, surface, weather, navigation stops, fitness, load, altitude, or trail conditions. The total distance should cover the whole outing; uphill gain means cumulative ascent, not net elevation change. Add a personal safety margin and check local trail conditions.

messages.checkInputs: Check the route distance, uphill gain, pace and break allowance.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: What pace does the Naismith-style baseline use?
additionalFaqs.answer: It uses 5 km/h for distance plus 10 minutes for every 100 m of cumulative uphill ascent. This traditional rule is only a simple baseline, not a guarantee for a particular trail or hiker.

additionalFaqs.question: Does the estimate include downhill terrain and trail difficulty?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It accounts for distance, cumulative ascent, the selected pace and planned breaks. It does not model descent, rough surfaces, technical terrain, weather, stops, fitness, altitude or trail conditions.

additionalFaqs.question: Should I enter one-way distance or the full outing?
additionalFaqs.answer: Enter the total distance for the entire outing. For an out-and-back hike, include both directions in the distance and enter cumulative uphill gain for the full planned outing.
